A Global Welcome to All Visitors – December 2025 Events in the United Arab Emirates 🇦🇪🌍

The United Arab Emirates warmly welcomes visitors from all around the world to the land of prosperity peace and innovation a nation that embraces everyone with tolerance respect and openness, embodying a global model of coexistence and progress.
To everyone arriving on the soil of the UAE welcome to the nation of the future where tomorrow is built today and every visitor is treated with honor and appreciation. 🤍

As December approaches, our nation proudly prepares to host a series of major national and international events:

🔸December 2 : 54th UAE National Day 🇦🇪

🔸December 3 : Tribes Day under the patronage and presence of the UAE 
President in Al Wathba – Abu Dhabi

🔸December 3–4 : BBW Dubai

🔸December 5–8: Formula 1 – Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 🏁

🔸December 8–9 : Bitcoin MENA Conference ₿

🔸 December 8–11 : Abu Dhabi Finance Week (ADFW) 💼

Traffic Advisory 🚗 :
Due to the overlap of these major events across Abu Dhabi and Dubai, heavy traffic is expected during this period.
We kindly advise all visitors to use public transportation whenever possible to avoid delays and ensure smooth mobility across the cities.

Welcome to the United Arab Emirates the land of vision unity and opportunity your safe destination toward a bright future

🚨12 HOUR NEWS RECAP

1.⁠ Trump urged Republican senators to “terminate the filibuster” and “open our country,” as the U.S government shutdown continued, calling on them to stop “playing games with the radical left” and push through his legislative agenda.

2.⁠ China launched its third aircraft carrier, the Fujian - its first fully homegrown ship equipped with electromagnetic catapults capable of launching J-35 stealth jets. The 80,000-ton vessel marks a major leap for Beijing’s navy.

3.⁠ Zohran Mamdani’s win has unleashed a wave of radical rhetoric from supporters vowing to “abolish police,” “dismantle borders,” and “put ICE agents on trial.” One viral post declared, “Woke Shariah is here.”

4.⁠ Trump floated giving Hungary exemptions from Russian oil sanctions, arguing the landlocked nation “has no ports” and “a difficult problem” securing energy elsewhere.

5.⁠ Zelensky praised Trump’s latest sanctions as “a very strong package,” saying they’re already squeezing Russia’s economy and defense sector while urging allies to keep tightening the pressure.

6.⁠ Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy dismissed viral theories about interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, saying it’s “just a comet” and that “humans love conspiracy theories” - not everything strange in the sky is aliens.

7.⁠ UPS grounded its entire MD-11 fleet effective immediately after the deadly Louisville crash that killed 14 people, saying the move is a precaution “in the interest of safety” following the manufacturer’s recommendation.

8.⁠ Sam Altman says OpenAI doesn’t need a bailout - just “a tiny loan guarantee” - after clarifying his CFO’s remarks on chip financing, insisting they’re not asking for handouts while juggling a $1.4 trillion vision and billion-dollar bills.

9.⁠ The Philippines is bracing for another super typhoon - Fung-wong (Uwan) - packing 185 kph winds and heading straight for Luzon just days after Typhoon Tino killed over 200 and left half a million without power.

10.⁠ More than 1,000 flights were canceled across the U.S as the FAA’s shutdown-related cuts hit 40 major airports - with air traffic controllers walking off unpaid shifts and airlines warning Thanksgiving could be chaos if towers stay empty.
